title: Identity compactification recovers direct image
statement:
If $f$ is proper, the identity compactification identifies $Rf_!^{(1,f)}$
with $Rf_*$, makes $\theta_1$ the identity, and identifies the compactified
formula with $\pi_{f,E,Q}$ and its inverse with $\rho_{f,E,Q}$.

proof.text: For the identity compactification $(j,p)=(1_X,f)$, the definition gives $Rf_!^{(1,f)}E=Rf_*j_!E$, canonically identified with $Rf_*E$. Under the identity-functor identifications, $j_!$ and $Lj^*$ and their unit constraints are identities. The canonical open-piece tensor map is then the identity map on $E\otimes^LLf^*Q$: its tensor and adjunction identity constraints have all become identities. Thus $\theta_1=1$ and $Rf_*\theta_1=Rf_*(\theta_1^{-1})=1$. Substituting into the displayed ordered composite gives $1\circ\pi_{f,E,Q}=\pi_{f,E,Q}$, and into the displayed reverse composite gives $\rho_{f,E,Q}\circ1=\rho_{f,E,Q}$. The maps $\pi$ and $\rho$ are the named projection-formula arrows, with $Q$ perfect as in the cited compactified formula; no new coefficient-category comparison is used.
